picks.headline: Feeling overwhelmed by the AI doom loop? Here's the essential reading list to make sense of it all
picks.excerpt: Guardian reporters and experts recommend the books that explain how the AI industry got here and where it is headed, amid a chaotic moment reshaping our lives.
picks.rationale: AI is the whole subject (45 mentions): a curated list of books about the AI industry. It is the only reader-facing item in the pool and a new outlet for the section, which balances the three scholarly-publishing picks.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: name specific titles and authors from the list and say what each helps a reader understand. Do not write a generic 'AI anxiety' piece.

picks.headline: Just Released: Clarivate Releases Pulse of the Library 2026
picks.excerpt: Clarivate's Pulse of the Library 2026 finds a widening gap between libraries actively implementing AI and those still experimenting; 16% globally report moderate-to-active AI implementation.
picks.rationale: AI adoption is the report's main finding, and it comes with hard numbers (16% of libraries worldwide at moderate-to-active AI implementation, and a widening gap). It is data, not opinion, so it beats the SK Groupthink essay for the last slot. infoDOCKET reaches its 2-card outlet cap here.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: lead with the numbers on the gap between libraries that are implementing AI and those still experimenting. The survey is vendor-published, so attribute findings to Clarivate. Keep it distinct from books-ital-genai-libraries (09-22) and books-crl-digitization (09-20): this card is about adoption rates, not integration case studies or digitization terms. This is the oldest item (09-09), so frame it as the current state of play.
